UC is saving ~₹35 crore per annum by using AI

Per UC’s Q4 FY26 filings, 55% of partner support queries are handled by AI. 

This has reduced the support cost per partner visit down from ~₹40 to ₹31.5 per order.

Voice AI plays a major role at UC in onboarding new partners, providing real-time query resolution during fixing and doing multi-way calls to coordinate visits.

Last month, Raghav Chandra, Co-Founder & CPTO of UC, demoed their AI assistant on stage at Mumbai Tech Week. 

He showed how UC’s AI assistant helped a service professional resolve a technical doubt while at the client’s home.

Their AI deployment scale is already meaningful:
1️⃣ 2.35 crore in-service job images processed Q4 FY26
2️⃣ 5 lakh call minutes handled in Q4 FY26
3️⃣ 100% of in-service images audited against SOPs in real time

Outside of partner enablement, UC is also using AI to improve its customer experience - placing filter reminder calls for Native, visualization of interiors in UC Revamp and much more.

➡️ For UC, the ₹35 crore of annualized savings represents a whopping 25% of the adjusted EBITDA figure in their core India biz. This is material & they are just getting started.

China built ‘Super Apps”. India is building “Super Companies”

In the late 2010s, it seemed like India would go down the same Super Apps route as China - every investor was looking for “India’s WeChat”

WhatsApp could never become WeChat for India. Paytm tried doing so with moderate success. Tata Neu burnt a ₹17000 crore hole trying to be everything to everyone.

In recent years, every major consumer internet platform in India has built a constellation of apps versus a Super App.

One super company with many focused apps and cross-app linkages (shared login, address & preferences) to improve customer experience. 

Pundits argued that crowded apps represented Indian bazaars therefore Super Apps would work in India 😂

An IIMA classroom project raised $1m today to offer authentic, affordable & domestically produced Ramen.

Nishank and Akhil observed that roadside vendors in Ahmedabad selling Korean ramen were quite successful. This led to an insight - if a snack is now available as street food, it has deep cultural penetration.

Customer feedback revealed that street ramen felt like ramen flavored masala noodles. The authentic alternatives were cup noodles which felt too processed or imported brands which are quite expensive (₹120 per packet).

This was their “Maggi Moment” - customers needed a semi-prepared packet which felt DIY but didn’t involve too much cooking (adding noodles + water + veggies).

The duo received a ₹14 Lakh grant from IIMA which allowed them to iterate for several months on the flavor profile by running a pop-up on campus. Once they locked this in, they began selling on Amazon & Flipkart - the reception was incredible - they made their first ₹8 Lakhs in sales.

AI is not replacing jobs. There is a fundamental difference between a collection of tasks & a job.

Job = U { Tasks, Judgment, Relationships, Context, Ownership}

Few jobs are truly at risk of replacement by AI - these involve more deterministic IO (Input Output) execution e.g. data entry, QA, CS etc.

Most jobs are resilient because:

(1) Human principals (business owners) always seek to assign responsibility & blame to a human agent.

(2) Deals get done not because of outbound spam but because of years of nurturing a relationship (showing up at conferences, events, meet-ups)

(3) The physical world is messy AF. Humans read non-verbal & subtle cues which are only possible via in-person interactions.

The midwits are right - AI is taking over tasks. In fact, if AI hasn’t taken over tasks for you then you’re doing something very wrong.

If tasks are automated & workflows are changing, jobs won’t be lost. In fact, to manage the messy transition, humans will be more in demand than ever before.

The data from Foundation Labs itself points to this (watch to the end of this rant)

Revenue has been stuck around ₹2,750 crore for the past 3 yrs

Lakmé was born in 1952 because South Delhi aunties protested in front of PM Nehru

Sounds absurd but there was a real problem: Post independence, our Govt restricted the import of non-essential products which included cosmetics to conserve our limited FOREX reserves.

Therefore, foreign products such as Hazeline Snow, Pond’s and Lux were no longer available on shelves.

Apart from Afghan Snow (Patanwala), there were few domestic alternatives. the South Delhi aunties had every right to protest 😆

The Lakmé story involves Independence, France, Tata Group & HUL ⤵️

I first met Aadit & KV on 6th January 2021 during our YC W21 office hours.

KiranaKart was delivering in a small radius within Bandra offering pick-ups from nearby kirana stores.

I was 20 kms away from their house but I couldn’t place an order.

One of our YC W21 batchmates told me: “Those Kirana dudes will get cooked by competition.”

5.5 yrs later, KiranaKart (now Zepto) is ready to IPO after filings its UDRHP. This is the fastest time from founding to IPO in our country in recent years.

Zepto fulfilled 64 crore orders in FY26 which translates to 23 Lakh orders per day in Q4 FY26🤯

I've met a dozen new VC fund managers in India this yr. One consistent theme across these meetings:

Their 1st hire is an "AI tinkerer" who is tasked with setting up an AI native system for the fund:

* CRM automations
* Mining & scraping pipeline
* Ops workflows

I have also observed that established funds have also begun actively hiring for this type of role.

Every fund manager has realized that several founder patterns can codified as external signals which are interpreted by LLMs

The tech renaissance come to VC world nearly 20 yrs after the HFT explosion hit the public markets.

As private markets deepen (esp. in India), Tech becomes a core competency for an investment institution.

Hence, you will see more fund managers hire for this skill set - which aligns with what has already taken place in the public markets.

Many partners have realized that 90% of the leg work can be done using AI.

This makes the prospect of starting up more alluring - esp. since they've all made some money from IPOs & are tired of doing team management, committee meetings and social pleasantries 

But, the remaining 10% of work (which is 90% of the job) still needs founder DNA to get out into the field, hustle hard & pursue opportunities.

For some, the allure of building an institution in a post AI era is worth the fees v/s carry trade-off.

But, for each of them who choose this path, they still go up against their former partners whom they have inadvertently empowered by freeing up more seats at the table.

IMHO, very good for the ecosystem - more funds means more cheque writers who will lead rounds (which is most needed in our country).

Balaji Wafers is the anti-thesis of India’s consumption narrative.

Started in 1984 as a potato wafers brand in Rajkot, Balaji is now a ₹6,500 crore revenue business with ~12% share of India’s salty snacks market.

The market narrative says: health-first, premiumization & pan-India distribution.

Balaji did exactly the opposite:

> Affordable instead of Premium
> Tasty instead of Healthy
> Regional density before Pan-India expansion

Due to this strategy, Balaji has grown 22.5% CAGR from FY20 to FY25 - much faster than the industry average of 15% CAGR

The Balaji story holds one key lesson ⤵️

Grandma stood up from the bed for the 1st time today approx. 45 days after her surgery

We still have a long journey ahead for her to stand unassisted and even longer (if at all) for her to walk again

When I met her in hospital, I promised her that we would all put in effort - she was afraid & didn't want to even try standing.

So I promised her, I wouldn't drink a single cup of coffee (which she knows I love) until she can walk again

If that means no coffee ever again, it is totally something I am okay with.

I told her: "We're all in" and after 4 long weeks of physio, this morning, it was a real delight to see standing (even if it was for 15 seconds with help)
